Tailwind v4 configured in apps/web

.env.example committed matching the infra doc's variable list
`wrangler dev` renders a placeholder page from apps/web and Hono responds on /api/*

stories.title: Seed the tier_limits catalog and dev/CI fixture users

acceptanceCriteria: `tier_limits` seeded with the v1 catalog (free: 5/3, plus: 60/30, pro: 250/120 for source_analysis/feedback_pass)

stories.title: Health check reports live database connectivity
stories.userStory: As the operator, I need a health check that proves the app can actually reach the database, not just that the process is up.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/health returns 200 including a live DB round-trip check
stories.notes: wrangler dev needs --env-file .env to bind DATABASE_URL (and the rest of .env) as Worker bindings locally/in CI, since Workers doesn't read .env automatically; production gets these via `wrangler secret put` per docs/infra.md. Added --env-file .env to pipeline.json's serve.dev/serve.ci, the root dev script, and the US-001 demo script. Unit tests mock createDb to cover both branches deterministically without a live DB/Docker dependency for `npm test`; the real live round trip is proven by this story's demo script against the real DATABASE_URL in .env. The per-request DB connection is deliberately left unclosed -- calling .end() races the Workers postgres.js polyfill's background stream read and surfaces as an unhandled rejection.

stories.title: CI test gate: typecheck/lint/build/test against a local Supabase Postgres service
stories.userStory: As a developer, I need CI to run the full check suite against a real Postgres service so tests that touch the database are trustworthy.
acceptanceCriteria: GitHub Actions workflow runs typecheck/lint/build/test on every PR against a local Supabase Postgres service

stories.title: Secret scanning in CI
stories.userStory: As the operator, I need every PR scanned for committed secrets so a leaked key is caught before merge, not after.
acceptanceCriteria: Secret scanning (e.g. gitleaks) runs in CI and fails the build on a match

stories.title: Deploy pipeline: migrate + wrangler deploy on merge, PR previews, secrets configured
stories.userStory: As a developer, I need merges to main to migrate and deploy automatically, and every PR to get a preview, so the pipeline can trust green builds and reviewers can see real changes running.
acceptanceCriteria: Merge to main runs migrations (drizzle-kit migrate + supabase db push) before wrangler deploy, and halts on migration failure
Every PR gets a Cloudflare Workers preview deployment with a posted-back URL, using dev-scoped secrets only
CI secrets (CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID, SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN, DATABASE_URL) configured in the GitHub Actions secrets store
Production app runtime secrets (SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY, LITELLM_API_KEY, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, etc.) bound to the Worker via `wrangler secret put`, never as plaintext `vars`

stories.title: Bootstrap first admin account
stories.userStory: As the operator, I need a way to mint the first admin account outside the normal approval flow, since approval itself requires an admin to already exist.
acceptanceCriteria: A documented, non-public script/CLI command (not an HTTP endpoint) promotes a specified email to role='admin', status='approved', creating the users/waitlist_signups rows if they don't yet exist
Requires direct DATABASE_URL access to run — cannot be triggered remotely or by an unauthenticated request
Documented in the README as the one-time production bootstrap step

stories.title: Verify rollback path (Worker + migration)
stories.userStory: As a developer, I need the rollback procedure actually exercised, not just documented, so a bad production deploy has a proven escape hatch.
acceptanceCriteria: A deliberately-broken deploy is rolled back via `wrangler rollback [deployment-id]` and the command output demonstrates the previous version serving again
A hand-written down-migration exists for at least one applied migration, documenting the emergency rollback procedure against DATABASE_URL
Rollback procedure documented in the README

stories.title: Global error handler + structured logging with correlation ID
stories.userStory: As a developer, I need every request's errors captured consistently so production issues are debuggable instead of guessed at.
acceptanceCriteria: Unhandled errors in any Hono route are caught by global middleware and returned as the standard { error: { code, message } } envelope, never a raw stack trace
Every request gets a correlation ID (generated or propagated from an incoming header), included in structured log output and in the error envelope
Server-side errors are logged with enough context (route, correlation ID, user ID if authenticated) to debug without reproducing

stories.title: Waitlist signup, admin approval, and login
stories.userStory: As a prospective user, I need to join a waitlist and log in once approved, so access is gated the way the product requires.
acceptanceCriteria: A visitor can submit the waitlist form (email + password) and sees a "pending approval" confirmation; a users row is created with status='pending'
A pending or rejected user who logs in sees a status screen ("pending approval" / "not approved") instead of the app
An admin can view the list of pending waitlist entries and approve or reject each one
Once approved, the same user can log in and reach the app (projects dashboard, empty state if no projects yet)
Waitlist/admin endpoints reject a non-admin caller with 403
Logout clears the session and a subsequent request to a protected route returns 401

stories.title: Password reset flow
stories.userStory: As a user, I need to reset my password if I forget it so I'm not permanently locked out of my account.
acceptanceCriteria: User can request a password reset via email; response is identical whether or not the email exists (no enumeration)
Reset link/token lets the user set a new password and log in with it
Expired or invalid reset tokens are rejected with a clear error
stories.notes: No email-sending infra exists yet, so /auth/password-reset/request relies on Supabase Auth's own mailer (supabase.auth.resetPasswordForEmail), reusing PUBLIC_APP_URL as the redirectTo. A custom recovery email template (supabase/templates/recovery.html + supabase/config.toml's [auth.email.template.recovery]) points the emailed link straight at our own /reset-password?token=<hash> instead of GoTrue's own /verify redirect, so the confirm step stays entirely backend-mediated via POST /auth/password-reset/confirm (verifyOtp + admin.updateUserById, which verified testing shows already revokes every other session for the user by itself -- an admin.signOut(..., 'global') call after it is defense-in-depth, not the primary mechanism, since authenticate() network-verifies every token via getUser() rather than decoding it locally; see middleware/auth.ts and docs/security.md), matching every other auth endpoint's frontend-never-talks-to-Supabase-directly convention. supabase/config.toml's redirect allow-list previously had no path/wildcard on it at all (locally or on the shared project), so GoTrue's exact-or-wildcard match silently fell back to site_url and dropped the /reset-password path on every reset link, with nothing surfacing the break -- config.toml now uses a local wildcard (`http://localhost:8787/**`) for `supabase start`, and deploy.yml's new "Push Supabase auth config" step (.github/scripts/push-supabase-auth-config.mjs) PATCHes just site_url/uri_allow_list on the shared dev/prod project via the Management API on every merge to main. Deliberately not `supabase config push`: that pushes the whole [auth] diff including the recovery template, and the shared project's free tier without custom SMTP rejects any email-template change with a 400, failing the entire push. The recovery template itself still only applies locally until the project has a paid plan or custom SMTP -- see docs/infra.md; that gap is now purely cosmetic (default GoTrue copy), not the functional break the missing wildcard was. In e2e/us-012.spec.ts, the initial request call is stubbed via page.route rather than hitting Supabase for real: two real resetPasswordForEmail calls during development were enough to 429 the shared dev project's auth-email quota for the rest of the hour, and this spec re-runs on every future PR per docs/testing.md's regression gate. That request/response contract (no-enumeration, 429 handling) is already exhaustively covered by mocked unit tests in apps/worker/src/routes/auth.test.ts; every other step in the e2e spec (token verification, password update, login) is a real call against the shared Supabase project.

stories.title: Admin user directory
stories.userStory: As an admin, I need to browse all users so I can answer support questions and audit accounts beyond just the waitlist queue.
acceptanceCriteria: Admin can search/filter all users by tier and status
Admin can view a user's basic info (email, status, role, tier, created_at)
Non-admin gets 403 on this view
Admin can revoke an already-approved user's access (status -> rejected); their next request is denied by the per-request status check
stories.notes: No subscriptions table exists yet (that is US-023/024's Stripe billing work) -- until then no account can be on a paid plan, so GET /admin/users returns tier: "free" for every user (a filter for plus/pro is a valid but always-empty query, not an error). Revoke reuses the waitlist_signups-mirrors-users.status invariant from docs/data-model.md via a new revokeUserAccess query, gated on the target currently being approved (409 not_approved otherwise). Also fixed a pre-existing playwright.config.ts gap: fullyParallel:false only serializes tests within one file, so separate spec files were still running concurrently (default worker count) and racing on the shared admin@example.test fixture session across files -- pinned workers:1 so cross-file demo specs sharing seeded fixture state (as the file already intended) actually run serially.

stories.title: Create, list, rename, and delete a project
stories.userStory: As a user, I need to create a paper project with a title and citation format so I have somewhere to gather sources and write.
acceptanceCriteria: Approved user can create a project with a title and citation format (MLA/APA/Chicago)
Citation format cannot be changed after creation (attempting to returns a clear error)
Projects dashboard lists the user's projects; empty state shown when none exist
User can rename a project and delete it (with confirmation)
A user cannot view or modify another user's project (403)

stories.title: Source discovery search
stories.userStory: As a user, I need to search for sources relevant to my paper so I don't have to find them all manually.
acceptanceCriteria: From a project, user can trigger a source search and see a list of candidate results (title, authors, year, venue, OA status)
An empty result set shows a clear empty state offering the manual-upload path
An upstream provider outage shows a clear error state, not a blank screen or raw error
Non-owner cannot search another user's project (403)

stories.title: Analyze a candidate source and select or reject it
stories.userStory: As a user, I need each candidate source summarized with strengths/weaknesses, a usefulness score, and key quotes, so I can decide whether to use it and add it to my bibliography.
acceptanceCriteria: User can trigger AI analysis on a candidate source and see the generated citation, strengths/weaknesses summary, usefulness score, and key quotes with usage suggestions
User can select an analyzed source into the bibliography; it appears in the project's bibliography view
User can reject a candidate; it does not reappear if the same search is re-run
A source lacking accessible full text is analyzed from its abstract and visibly flagged as abstract-only, not shown as an error
Deselecting a selected source returns it to the candidate pool rather than deleting it
Analysis is blocked with a clear limit-reached response once the user's tier quota for source analyses is exhausted

stories.title: Upload your own PDF/TXT source
stories.userStory: As a user, I need to upload my own source document so I can use material the automated search doesn't find.
acceptanceCriteria: User can upload a PDF or TXT file (≤ configured size limit) as a source; it's automatically analyzed and added to the bibliography
Uploading an unsupported file type or oversized file is rejected with a clear, specific error
A corrupted or unparseable file fails gracefully with a clear error, not a crash or silent empty analysis
A scanned-image-only PDF with no extractable text is flagged as such rather than analyzed on empty content

stories.title: Editor: load, edit, and autosave a document in TipTap
stories.userStory: As a user, I need to open my project in a rich text editor and have my edits saved automatically, so I never lose work.
acceptanceCriteria: Opening a project loads its document into the rich text editor and autosaves edits

stories.title: Citation-format rendering: in-text citations, full-document re-render, dangling-citation detection
stories.userStory: As a user, I need in-text citations and the full paper to render correctly for my chosen citation style, so I don't have to format manually.
acceptanceCriteria: Inserting an in-text citation from the bibliography renders it correctly formatted for the project's citation style
Triggering a full re-render assembles the complete formatted paper (headers/margins/bibliography page) per the project's style
A re-render flags any in-text citation whose source is no longer in the bibliography (dangling citation)
Citation formatting is visually distinct per format (MLA vs. APA vs. Chicago) for the same source

stories.title: Paragraph and structure suggestions in the editor
stories.userStory: As a user, I need suggestions on how to start a paragraph or structure a section, so I have a starting point without the tool writing for me.
acceptanceCriteria: While writing, the user can request paragraph/structure suggestions relevant to their current position; suggestions appear as inline, non-inserted hints
Suggestions are not counted against the user's metered usage (only rate-limited)
Rapid repeated requests are throttled with a clear rate-limit response, not silently dropped

stories.title: Post-writing feedback pass
stories.userStory: As a user, I need feedback on wording, phrasing, grammar, and content after I write, so I can revise my own draft without the tool writing for me.
acceptanceCriteria: User can request a feedback pass on their current draft and see wording/phrasing/grammar/content comments anchored to specific spans in the editor, rendered as margin-style annotations
Nothing is auto-applied to the document — comments are advisory only
User can view the history of past feedback passes and reopen an earlier one
Requesting a feedback pass on an empty document returns a clear error instead of an empty/nonsensical pass
Feedback is blocked with a clear limit-reached response once the user's tier quota for feedback passes is exhausted

stories.title: Usage dashboard and limit-exceeded UX
stories.userStory: As a user, I need to see my current usage against my plan's limits so I understand why an action was blocked and what to do about it.
acceptanceCriteria: User can see their current usage (source analyses, feedback passes used/remaining) and plan tier
Attempting a metered action after exhausting the tier's monthly limit shows a clear "upgrade or wait" message rather than a generic error
Usage resets at the next billing period boundary
Tier limits reflect the seeded v1 catalog (free 5/3, plus 60/30, pro 250/120)

stories.title: Stripe Checkout and Billing Portal
stories.userStory: As a user, I need to upgrade my subscription and manage billing so I can get higher usage limits.
acceptanceCriteria: User can start a Stripe Checkout session to upgrade to Plus or Pro and, on success, their tier updates to match
User can open the Stripe Billing Portal to manage/cancel their subscription
A user already on a tier cannot start a duplicate checkout for the same tier (clear error)
stories.notes: Resuming from needs_human per steering (issue #1 comment 2026-08-15): Stripe blocker in #54 confirmed cleared (POST /v1/checkout/sessions now returns a session url). Rebasing feature/us-023-stripe-checkout-and-billing-portal onto main and renumbering its migration from 0008 to 0012 (main now owns 0008-0011), regenerating the snapshot rather than reusing the stale one.

stories.title: Stripe webhook sync: subscription status, payment-failure grace period, signature verification
stories.userStory: As the operator, I need Stripe webhook events to keep our billing state in sync reliably, so tier access always matches what the customer is actually paying for.
acceptanceCriteria: Webhook endpoint is registered for exactly these events: checkout.session.completed, customer.subscription.created, customer.subscription.updated, customer.subscription.deleted, invoice.payment_failed
checkout.session.completed links the session's subscription/customer IDs to the initiating user via client_reference_id or metadata set at session creation
customer.subscription.created/updated/deleted keep subscriptions.status, current_period_start/end, and cancel_at_period_end in sync with Stripe, idempotent under redelivery

invoice.payment_failed does not immediately downgrade the user; past_due/failed-payment users keep their active tier through a grace period, downgrading only once Stripe reports the subscription canceled/unpaid
An invalid webhook signature is rejected and never triggers a tier change
stories.notes: Demoed via signed fixture events POSTed directly to the webhook route (per docs/testing.md), not a browser flow -- there is no user-visible page for webhook delivery itself.

stories.title: Read-only share link
stories.userStory: As a user, I need to share a read-only link to my paper (e.g. with an instructor) without giving them edit access or an account.
acceptanceCriteria: Owner can generate a read-only share link for a project and revoke it
Visiting a valid share link (no login) shows the paper's title, bibliography, and content, with no editing affordances
A revoked or unknown share link shows a clear "this link no longer works" state, not an error page or the owner's other data
Generating a link twice returns the existing active link rather than creating a second one
stories.notes: share_links.token_hash (column name kept for schema/migration parity with docs/data-model.md) stores the raw high-entropy token, not a SHA-256 digest, despite that doc's "plaintext shown once" annotation -- AC4 ("generating a link twice returns the existing active link") requires the token to be retrievable on repeat GET/POST calls, which a hash-only column can't support. Chose functional correctness per the acceptance criteria; entropy (256-bit random) plus revocation plus the read-only single-project blast radius (docs/security.md's threat note) is the actual defense, consistent with how this codebase already does manual per-request ownership checks rather than the anon-key+RLS path docs/data-model.md originally sketched. Also fixed a real bug while building this: share_links.createdBy was missing onDelete: cascade (every other users.id FK in the schema has it), which blocked deleting a user who had ever created a share link -- caught via a genuine Supabase admin.deleteUser 500 during e2e cleanup, fixed before the migration was applied anywhere. Separately, drizzle-kit migrate silently exits 1 against this shared dev DB (pre-existing __drizzle_migrations bookkeeping gaps from prior stories, unrelated to this change) -- applied the migration SQL directly and recorded matching bookkeeping rows by hand; worth a look if a future story hits the same silent failure. Local e2e regression pass also hit two unrelated, pre-existing flaky specs (US-012, US-016) that intermittently exceed their default 30s timeout in this sandbox's network path to the shared dev Supabase project -- neither touches any code this story changed; US-025's own spec passed cleanly on every run once given test.slow() (added here, matching e2e/us-021.spec.ts's precedent for longer flows).

stories.title: RLS integration test suite (deny-by-default across roles)
stories.userStory: As a developer, I need proof at the database level — not just the API layer — that RLS denies cross-user access, so a bug in one layer doesn't leave the other undefended.
acceptanceCriteria: Integration tests prove an authenticated non-owner cannot read or write another user's projects, sources, documents, or feedback passes, with RLS denying it even bypassing the API layer
Integration tests prove a pending/rejected user's JWT is denied by RLS, not just by API middleware
Integration tests prove the share-link read path exposes only the single linked project and nothing else
Every table reachable via the anon key has RLS enabled — a lint/test step fails the build if a new table is added without it

stories.title: Rate limiting on public and metered endpoints
stories.userStory: As the operator, I need public and AI-cost-bearing endpoints rate-limited so a script can't run up API cost or abuse signup faster than the tier quota alone would prevent.
acceptanceCriteria: Public auth endpoints (signup, login, password-reset request) are rate-limited per IP with a clear 429 response
Metered AI endpoints (analyze, feedback) are rate-limited per user in addition to the tier-quota check
A user hitting the rate limit sees a clear "try again shortly" message with a Retry-After value

stories.title: Timeout and retry/backoff policy for outbound calls
stories.userStory: As the operator, I need outbound calls to external APIs to fail fast and retry sanely so a slow provider doesn't hang requests or silently double-charge usage.
acceptanceCriteria: Calls to Semantic Scholar, CrossRef, Unpaywall, and the LiteLLM proxy have an explicit timeout and don't hang the request indefinitely
Transient failures (timeout, 5xx) are retried with backoff before surfacing an error to the user
Retries never double-charge a user's metered quota or double-write a result

stories.title: Accessibility and responsive-layout hardening
stories.userStory: As a user relying on keyboard navigation, assistive tech, or a smaller screen, I need the core flows to actually work for me, not just for a mouse on a desktop browser.
acceptanceCriteria: Core flows (signup, project creation, source review, editor, feedback, checkout) are completable via keyboard alone, with visible focus order
Interactive elements have accessible names/labels, verified via automated accessibility audit
Core flows render usably at mobile and desktop viewport widths without horizontal scrolling or hidden controls

stories.title: README and docs finalized
stories.userStory: As a developer joining later, I need setup/run/test/deploy documented accurately so I can get productive without reverse-engineering CI.
acceptanceCriteria: README documents setup, running locally, running tests, and deploying, matching what CI actually does
Every environment variable in .env.example has a one-line purpose note in the README or links to the infra doc
Architecture/decisions doc is linked from the README for anyone picking up the project later
Backup/restore procedure documented: relying on Supabase-managed Postgres backups (see docs/infra.md); noted as an operational runbook item to revisit before scaling past bootstrap budget
